HiTHIUM Highlights 8-Hour LDES Storage and Local Expansion at All Energy Australia

Energy storage technology provider HiTHIUM presented its latest long-duration energy storage (LDES) systems and local support capabilities at the All Energy Australia exhibition in Melbourne on October 28. The company highlighted its 8-hour native battery energy storage system alongside grid compliance tools and regional service developments designed to meet Australia's changing grid requirements.

Shifting Market Dynamics Toward Longer Durations

As Australia's energy market evolves, grid flexibility and supply reliability have become increasingly critical. Federal initiatives like the Capacity Investment Scheme, alongside state-level efforts such as New South Wales' dedicated LDES tenders, continue to generate momentum for longer-duration storage assets.

According to market data cited by HiTHIUM, high-price events in Australia have lengthened, with pricing events lasting four hours or longer accounting for over 70% of scarcity revenue in 2025. Furthermore, analysis from CSIRO GenCost indicates that deploying two separate 4-hour systems to achieve an 8-hour output would carry a capital cost approximately 23% higher than a purpose-built 8-hour system.

Technology and Grid Compliance Features

At the Melbourne event, the company featured its ∞Power 6.9MWh 8-hour-native BESS, housed in a standard 20-foot container. The system boasts up to 96% round-trip efficiency, a 25-year design life, and compatibility with power conversion systems (PCS) and energy management systems (EMS) from major global manufacturers. HiTHIUM states that the configuration reduces land use by 15% compared to standard 4-hour setups and meets key NFPA, IEC, and AS safety standards.

To address complex interconnection procedures, the firm also demonstrated its Grid Compliance Simulation and Verification Platform. The software assists projects through various compliance phases—from R0 and R1 assessments to commissioning and R2 model validation—using automated simulation and hardware-in-the-loop testing to mitigate late-stage project risks.

Localized Partnerships and Service Expansion

Beyond utility-scale hardware, HiTHIUM showcased its ∞Power 1022kWh liquid-cooled commercial and industrial (C&I) cabinet utilizing ∞Cell 1175Ah LDES cells, alongside the HeroEE 16 and ARKVOLT F8S residential product series.

To support its expanding footprint, HiTHIUM is developing a nationwide service network covering spare-parts warehousing, training, maintenance, and battery recycling. During the exhibition, the company signed strategic cooperation agreements with industry partners including Raystech and Ingeteam. Additionally, HiTHIUM announced that its dedicated Brisbane service center is slated to open by mid-2027 to provide closer regional support.

Practical Implications and Verification

Readers, industry participants, and developers tracking the Australian energy storage market should consider several practical factors when evaluating these developments:

  • Confirmed Details: HiTHIUM officially exhibited its ∞Power 6.9MWh 8-hour BESS, C&I cabinets, residential lines, and its Grid Compliance platform at All Energy Australia on October 28. The company also announced strategic agreements with Raystech and Ingeteam, plus a planned Brisbane service center opening by mid-2027.
  • Uncertainties: Specific commercial deployment volumes, project financial terms, and the exact operational timelines for individual partner agreements were not disclosed in the announcement.
  • Relevant Comparisons: The reported CSIRO GenCost findings suggest economic advantages for dedicated 8-hour systems over stacked 4-hour configurations when addressing extended scarcity pricing events.
  • How to Verify: Interested readers can review the official corporate announcement and details regarding the exhibition directly through the PR Newswire Source.
